newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico expected to create petrochemical divisions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico expected to create petrochemical divisions.

text.p: Mexico's state-owned oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) is expected to formally create 10 petrochemical companies as a preliminary step in the sale of a minority stake of the plants, a company spokeswoman said Thursday.
She said the company plans Friday to make an announcement in Cosoleacaque, Veracruz state, the site of Mexico's top petrochemical producing plant.
Energy minister Jesus Reyes Heroles said last week companies would be invited to bid for a 49 percent stake in the 10 plants in the second half of the year.
The first four plants designated for privatization are: Cosoleacaque, Escolin in the Poza Rica plant in Veracruz, Tula in Hidalgo state and Camargo in Chihuahua state.

Cosoleacaque had a petrochemical output of 4.9 million tonnes of a total 19.18 million tonnes in 1994. Escolin produced 280,000 tonnes, Tula produced 59,000 tonnes and Camargo produced 346,000 tonnes for the year, according to the latest Pemex data.
